{{Short description|Croatian-Italian mathematician (1808–1883)}}
[[File:Serafino Rafaele Minich.jpg|thumb|Serafino Raffaele Minich]]
'''Serafino Raffaele Minich''' or '''Serafin Rafael Minić''' (8 December 1808 – 29 May 1883) was a [[Croatia]]n-[[Italy|Italian]] mathematician.<ref name="HE">{{citation |contribution-url=https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/minic-serafin-rafael |contribution=Minić, Serafin Rafael |title=[[Croatian Encyclopedia]] |year=1999–2009 |access-date=January 2, 2014 |publisher=[[Leksikografski zavod Miroslav Krleža]] |language=Croatian}}</ref>

Minić was born in [[Venice]]. His father, a sea captain from [[Prčanj]], settled in the early nineteenth century in Venice where Minić has spent his entire life. After receiving a degree in mathematics at the [[University of Padua]], in 1830 he started working at the University as an assistant, and since 1842 as a lecturer.<ref name="HE"/>

During his lifetime, he served as the [[Rector (academia)|rector]] of the [[University of Padua]], [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the Faculty of Arts, dean of the Faculty of Science, and for several years he led the [[Istituto di scienze, letere ed arti]] in Venice.<ref name="HE"/>

He published more than 60 papers in the theory of [[differential equations]], [[algebra]], [[mechanics]] and [[hydraulics]]. In 1875–76 he led the project of altering the port on [[Lido di Venezia|Lido]] in [[Venice]] and regulating the flow of the river [[Brenta (river)|Brenta]]. He wrote several treatises on [[Dante Alighieri|Dante]], [[Petrarch]] and [[Torquato Tasso|Tasso]]. In the hall of the University of Padua a memorial is raised in his honor.<ref name="HE"/>

He died in [[Venice]].
